title: Gold Prices Today: 24K Gold Slips ₹160 to ₹1.49 Lakh as Festive Season Buying Begins
excerpt: 24K gold eased to around ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams on Tuesday, October 6, after Monday's sharper ₹1,100 drop; silver held near ₹2.25 lakh per kg across major cities.
body:
• 24K gold eased about ₹160 per 10 grams on Tuesday, quoted near ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams in most Indian cities, extending the slide that began with a ₹1,100 drop on Monday.
  • City-wise, 24K gold ranged from ₹148,850 (New Delhi) to ₹149,620 (Chennai) per 10 grams; 999-fine silver ranged from ₹224,900 to ₹226,090 per kilogram.
  • At today's 22K rate of roughly ₹1,36,600 per 10 grams, a 20-gram bangle carries about ₹2.73 lakh in metal value alone — before making charges (often 8–18% of the metal value) and 3% GST. Festive and wedding-season buyers should compare making charges across jewellers and verify BIS hallmarking before purchasing.
  • Traders in Delhi described demand as subdued, while the Nifty traded firm around 22,650 and the dollar-rupee futures contract hovered near ₹96.61, keeping bullion on the back foot.

Gold prices in India edged lower on Tuesday, October 6, as 24-karat gold (99.9% purity) slipped to about ₹14,902 per gram in most cities, with 22-karat (91.6% purity) quoted near ₹13,660 per gram and 18-karat at ₹11,177 per gram, according to market tracker data compiled by Goodreturns.in and reported by HDFC Sky. The 24K rate fell ₹16 per gram from Monday's level — a decline of about 0.11%, or ₹160 per 10 grams — extending the slide that set in last week and carried through a ₹1,100-per-10-gram drop on Monday.

The softer trend comes at a notable moment: India's festive and wedding season is underway, traditionally the strongest period for retail gold demand, and traders are watching closely to see whether lower prices draw buyers back to showrooms.

City-wise gold and silver rates on October 6

Retail rates varied modestly across metros, according to data reported by Livemint. Delhi again carried the highest 24K rate at ₹14,917 per gram — a ₹15 premium over the Mumbai cluster at ₹14,902 — while Ahmedabad and Vadodara held a smaller ₹5-per-gram premium at ₹14,907. Chennai's 18K rate stood at ₹11,220 per gram against ₹11,177 in the Mumbai cluster.

"Domestic prices near ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams remain close to record territory, which itself may explain the subdued retail demand traders are reporting."

Silver largely held its ground. The 999-fine metal was quoted between ₹224,900 and ₹226,090 per kilogram across the six cities, even as ThePrint reported that gold and silver prices remained flat in Delhi amid subdued demand.

Why prices are easing

The decline is mild compared with Monday's sharp ₹1,100-per-10-gram fall in 24K gold, but it keeps the metal on the back foot at the start of the week. Gold prices in India track international bullion rates and the dollar-rupee exchange rate, so even modest daily moves reflect how global cues and the currency settled overnight.

Broader markets painted a mixed backdrop. The Nifty 50 was firmer in late-morning trading, around 22,650 — up about 0.43% — which tends to draw some safe-haven flows away from bullion. The USDINR futures contract expiring October 28 was quoted near ₹96.61; a steady-to-strong dollar against the rupee typically weighs on domestic gold because the metal is priced in dollars internationally.

Behind the day-to-day moves sits a longer rally. Gold has climbed through 2026 as geopolitical uncertainty, central-bank buying, and expectations around global interest rates pushed investors toward the metal. Domestic prices near ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams remain close to record territory, which itself may explain the subdued retail demand traders are reporting.

What it means for festive-season buyers

For households buying ahead of Diwali and the wedding season, the metal value is only part of the bill. A 22K bangle or necklace typically carries making charges that vary widely between jewellers — commonly 8–18% of the metal value for machine-made pieces, with flat per-gram rates at traditional smiths — plus 3% GST on the total. On a ₹2.73-lakh metal bill for 20 grams of 22K gold, that difference can mean tens of thousands of rupees depending on where you buy.

For NRIs flying home for weddings or the festive season, gold is often a standard purchase during the visit — and at these levels it deserves the same diligence as any large financial decision. Verify the BIS hallmark — the BIS logo, a purity grade such as "22K916," and the unique six-digit alphanumeric HUID code, which can be checked on the BIS Care app — and insist on a detailed invoice showing the metal weight, making charges, and GST separately.

Buyers with a long horizon should also remember that 24K gold (99.9% purity) is better suited to coins and bars because of its softness, while 22K (91.6% purity) is the standard for jewellery; comparing like with like is the first step to a fair deal.

What's next

In the near term, traders will watch international bullion cues, the dollar-rupee rate, and US economic data for direction. Whether the mild correction is enough to revive retail demand will become clear over the coming weeks, as jewellers enter the heart of the festive buying calendar. If global risk appetite continues to firm, gold's record run could pause further; if geopolitical or economic anxiety returns, the metal has historically been the first place investors look.
